analysis: The recurrent-memory experiment succeeded with host-evaluated macro validation HR@10 of 0.535, exceeding the stated 0.505 reference by 0.030 absolute. Category HR@10 was 0.610 for Movies_and_TV, 0.570 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.395 for Electronics, and 0.565 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remains the weakest category. The result supports further investigation of recurrent history modeling, but this trial does not isolate the benefit of the GRU, cumulative memory, or ranking objective. No test performance is available.
code_summary: Trains one independent RecurrentMemory network per category with seed 42. Each network combines shared item embeddings, a GRU, the current item representation, and a gated cumulative-history mean through one normalized scoring representation and learned item bias. Training supervises next-item transitions using 32 sampled negatives, pairwise softplus ranking loss, auxiliary positive/negative logistic losses, and AdamW. Checkpoints are selected by validation HR@10, with NDCG breaking ties. The exported predictor reproduces the architecture and routes each category to exactly one checkpoint; no ensemble or separately fitted scoring component is used.
